summary: VertexPay midnight routing fallbacks triggered — increased latency, streaming disconnects, and embedding-score regression
description: Issue summary: Between 00:30 and 02:10 UTC on 2026-03-13 VertexPay experienced repeated fallback routing events which caused elevated token latency (p50 -> 3x normal) and intermittent streaming disconnects for production traffic. In parallel, customers reported embedding score regressions against a pinned model used for fraud detection. Impact: VertexPay (enterprise account) observed increased error rates for streaming sessions ~7% and a 30% increase in end-to-end request latency, which caused batch reconciliation jobs to miss SLAs. Timeline: 00:28 first routing timeouts detected by SLO alert; 00:35 automated routing fallback kicked in; 00:50 VertexPay opened support escalation; 01:15 hotfix deployed to reduce fallback aggressiveness; 02:05 monitoring shows stabilization. Customer impact: degraded UX for product users, delayed reconciliation jobs, and concern about embedding drift. Business impact: potential SLA credit, P0 escalation with CSM in loop.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use VertexPay account with pinned model redwood-open-7B-v2 in us-east region
2) Generate sustained request traffic with small messages (avg seq len 64) and a mix of streaming and non-streaming calls at 150% of normal baseline
3) Observe routing controller logs for fallback events and increased per-token latency
4) Run embedding comparisons against baseline vectors to reproduce score variance (see logs)

comments: 2026-03-13 00:45 - Priya Singh (Support): Opened P0 and paged SRE. Notified CSM and assigned incident lead. Asked VertexPay for recent request ids.
2026-03-13 00:50 - Omar Diaz (SRE): Initial hypothesis: autoscaler under-provisioned GPU pool leading to slower downstream responses, triggering the routing controller's fallback threshold.

2026-03-13 01:05 - Maya Chen (Runtime Eng): Found a recent routing-config rollout (PR 1764) that lowered backend timeout threshold from 800ms to 500ms in us-east. Rolling back to previous threshold for vertexpay-prod as emergency mitigation.
2026-03-13 01:18 - Priya Singh (Support): Communicated mitigation to VertexPay and requested verification on their end. Customer confirmed improved streaming experience for a subset of sessions.

2026-03-13 02:10 - Miguel Alvarez (CSM): Customer acknowledged stabilization and asked for a summary and follow-up on embedding score regression investigations. Marking incident as resolved pending post-incident review.
2026-03-14 09:12 - Priya Singh (Support): Scheduled post-incident review with VertexPay and internal teams for 2026-03-16. Action items captured below.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: Routing timeout change in PR 1764 reduced tolerance for transient backend latency spikes leading to more frequent fallbacks.
Hypothesis B: Autoscaler had insufficient warm capacity during nightly traffic shift; GPU provisioning lag observed in scaling logs between 00:29-00:36.
Evidence: Autoscaler logs show scale-up request at 00:30 but new nodes not ready until 00:44. Serving runtime hot-path showed increased GPU queue depth and slow kv-cache hits at the same window.

Embedding regression: upstream quantization experiment for embedding-adam-512 (PR 889) had a canary that overlapped with VertexPay's traffic window. Batch tests show mean-similarity drop of ~0.12; needs separate A/B analysis.
Slack threads: #support (t: March 13 00:48) and #infra-incidents thread INC-2026-0313-09
resolution_notes: 1) Immediate: Rolled back routing-controller timeout change for vertexpay-prod (reverted PR 1764) at 01:08 UTC which reduced unnecessary fallbacks.
2) Autoscaler: Increased warm pool minimum for Dedicated GPU pool serving enterprise traffic during midnight windows. Hotfix deployed 01:40 UTC to speed node provisioning path.
3) Embeddings: Disabled canary quantization for embedding-adam-512 for VertexPay until A/B analysis completes. Reverted PR 889 canary flag at 01:55 UTC.

4) Communication: Notified VertexPay of mitigations and provided initial incident timeline and next steps. CSM offered a follow-up review call and potential SLA credit depending on postmortem findings.
5) Post-incident actions created: runbook updates for routing timeout rollout, autoscaler warm pool policy, embedding canary gating for enterprise customers. Owners assigned in follow-up meeting.
